codeReview.summary: The ios_app_harness binary implementation is comprehensive and correctly wired into the meson.build system. The implementation creates a new test harness executable at tests/cases/harness/ios_app_harness.c that implements 6 APPSIM test cases (APPSIM-001 through APPSIM-006). The meson.build changes properly declare the executable and wire it into the test suite with appropriate suite tags (phase-02b-ios-simulator-harness, bootstrap, gate) and timeouts. The binary successfully links against libish_emu as required.

sharedStateObservations.observation: The ios_app_harness.c uses system() and popen() calls with shell commands (xcodebuild, xcrun simctl) rather than using XcodeBuildMCP tools directly. This is acceptable for a test harness that runs outside the MCP context, but it's a notable deviation from the AGENTS.md convention which specifies 'Use XcodeBuildMCP tools - Never use xcodebuild or simctl directly'. However, since this is a compiled C harness that runs as a meson test, it cannot directly invoke MCP tools and the shell command approach is appropriate.
sharedStateObservations.evidence: tests/cases/harness/ios_app_harness.c:340-350 - uses xcodebuild command via exec_cmd_to_file(); tests/cases/harness/ios_app_harness.c:380-390 - uses xcrun simctl commands

sharedStateObservations.observation: The harness correctly follows the explicit test declaration pattern from the existing codebase. All 6 APPSIM tests are explicitly declared in tests/cases/meson.build with proper suite tags, timeouts, and is_parallel: false (appropriate for simulator tests that cannot run concurrently).

The worker discovered the correct pattern for implementing test harnesses in this codebase: (1) create harness C file with case routing logic, (2) add executable declaration in harness/meson.build, (3) add explicit test declarations in cases/meson.build. This pattern is consistent with existing harnesses like ios_fixture_harness and semantic_micro_harness.
sharedStateObservations.evidence: Transcript shows worker examined existing harness files (ios_fixture.c, semantic_micro_harness) before implementing ios_app_harness.c

sharedStateObservations.observation: The services.yaml already contains XcodeBuildMCP configuration which the harness uses as defaults. The harness hardcodes values from services.yaml (DEFAULT_SIMULATOR_ID, DEFAULT_BUNDLE_ID, etc.) which is appropriate for a test harness.
sharedStateObservations.evidence: .factory/services.yaml contains simulator_id: E6186E89-8784-473B-A4E4-66E42693F14E and bundle_id: com.rudironsoni.ish; tests/cases/harness/ios_app_harness.c defines matching DEFAULT_SIMULATOR_ID and DEFAULT_BUNDLE_ID
